note: Habitats a visitor can be briefed for. `id` matches game.js reef.biome (biomes advance in order; after the last, cycle). Add freely; the pipeline reads this, nothing is hardcoded. `pass_through`: scenery kinds creatures may swim/fly through in this biome (default none: everything registered is solid). Kinds: rock, coral, anemone, shrub, plus any new scenery's kind. `scene`: which scenery set habitat.js builds (reef, kelp, tidepool, mangrove, deep, meadow, canopy; default by medium). A new scene needs its builder in habitat.js `tiers` and colors in `LOOKS`. `look`: the biome's identity (see `identity_rules`); briefs, habitat.js and the shelf diorama all read it.

look.shape: branching and plated: antler corals, tables, fans, round brain domes
look.creatures: laterally flat, disc-shaped or chunky reef fish and turtles; bold bands, spots and saddles in saturated warm-and-cool pairs (orange/white, yellow/blue)
look.plants: reef algae, calcified fronds, polyp-like tufts in coral pinks and lime
look.motion: busy darting, quick turns, hovering in place

look.shape: vertical ribbons floor to surface; long gas-bladdered stipes
look.ground: dark cobble and boulders, urchin barrens
look.creatures: elongated, camouflaged or single loud color (garibaldi orange); leaf-like flaps, bristles, spines; olive, gold, rust
look.plants: long blades, bladders, holdfasts in olive, amber and brown
look.motion: slow sway with the swell, hanging in the current

look.shape: rock rims and round pools seen close; clustered shells
look.ground: dark wet granite with pools of clear water
look.creatures: small, low and sticky: crabs, stars, slugs, sculpins; frilly nudibranch ruffles; electric purple, ochre, hot pink, emerald
look.plants: encrusting, tufted, rubbery: coralline pink, surfgrass, sea lettuce
look.motion: still, then a quick scuttle; clinging

look.shape: arching prop roots and tangled verticals over mud
look.ground: soft brown mud, leaf litter, tannin water
look.creatures: amphibious and bug-eyed: mudskippers, crabs with one big claw, archers; mottled mud browns with one bright flash (blue, yellow)
look.plants: leathery waxy leaves, pencil roots, seed pods in olive and tan
look.motion: perch, hop, pause; lazy in murky water

look.shape: translucent bells, long trailing strings, sparse points of light in black
look.ground: near-black silt, almost no floor visible
look.creatures: translucent, gelatinous, big-mouthed or long-bodied; glowing photophores and lures; black, deep red, violet, with cyan points of light
look.plants: pale glass spires, ghostly stalks, whip coral
look.motion: drift and pulse, very slow, long pauses

look.shape: soft rolling mounds and upright stems with round flower heads
look.creatures: fuzzy and round: bees, hares, beetles, butterflies; warm yellows, pinks, soft browns, polka dots
look.plants: daisy, poppy and lupine forms; round heads on upright stems; sunny warm colors
look.motion: flitting, bobbing, hopping in short bursts

look.shape: horizontal mossy limbs with clouds below; things perched and clinging
look.ground: no floor: thick mossy branches above a cloud sea
look.creatures: perchers and clingers: hummingbirds, tree frogs, sloths; iridescent greens and jewel tones
look.plants: orchids, mosses, air plants, hanging epiphytes; pale petals, jewel accents
look.motion: hover and cling; slow hang, quick hover

biomes.name: Jungle understory
biomes.light: deep green shade, god rays through gaps

look.shape: giant leaves and buttress trunks; everything big, layered and dripping
look.creatures: warning colors on dark green: dart-frog reds, blues and yellows, toucan beaks, glossy beetles; big eyes, long limbs for climbing
look.plants: huge split or paddle leaves, red bromeliad rosettes, pitcher plants; dark glossy greens with one hot accent
look.motion: still and watchful, then a sudden leap or climb

identity_rules: Each biome owns one SHAPE LANGUAGE (e.g. branching, vertical ribbons, rounded clusters, arching roots, hanging, horizontal limbs). Its scenery and its creatures echo that shape; no other biome uses it as its main shape.
Each biome owns a HUE FAMILY (`look.palette`: sky/water, depth/horizon, ground, accent). Pick creature and plant colors from or next to it; avoid the main hues of the neighboring biomes.
`look.owns` lists motifs only this biome may use (scenery, creatures, plants). Never use a motif another biome owns.
Swap test: if this design would look at home in another biome with only a recolor, redesign it. Change at least two of: body plan, silhouette, pattern type, hue family, size class, motion.
Silhouette test: filled solid black at card size, the design should still say which biome it is from.
Motion signature (`look.motion`) sets the idle feel: match it (a deep creature drifts and pulses, a meadow one flits).
